topic.subject: science
topic.title: Carbon and its compounds
topic.scope: covalent bonding, versatility of carbon, hydrocarbons, functional groups, ethanol, ethanoic acid, soaps and detergents

misconceptions.statement: Covalent bonds are formed by the transfer of electrons from one atom to another.
misconceptions.why: Students often confuse covalent bonding with ionic bonding because they learn both simultaneously.
misconceptions.fix: Covalent bonds are formed by the mutual sharing of electron pairs between atoms to achieve a stable electronic configuration.

probe.question: How does a chlorine atom achieve stability when forming a molecule of Cl2?
probe.wrong_answer: One chlorine atom gives an electron to the other chlorine atom.

misconceptions.statement: Atoms share electrons to become like the nearest noble gas by filling their shells completely.
misconceptions.why: Textbooks emphasize 'full shells' which leads students to think atoms must have 8 electrons regardless of the shell level.
misconceptions.fix: Atoms share electrons to attain the stable electronic configuration of the nearest noble gas, which for hydrogen means a duplet, not an octet.

probe.question: Does a hydrogen atom need 8 electrons in its valence shell to be stable?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, all atoms need 8 electrons to complete their octet.

misconceptions.statement: Carbon is the only element that can form chains and rings.
misconceptions.why: The curriculum focuses heavily on carbon's catenation, leading students to believe it is unique in this ability.
misconceptions.fix: While carbon shows catenation to a high degree, other elements like silicon and sulfur can also form chains and rings.

probe.question: Can any other element besides carbon form long chains?
probe.wrong_answer: No, only carbon has the property of catenation.

misconceptions.statement: A functional group is just a label for a part of a molecule and does not change its chemical properties.
misconceptions.why: Students often memorize functional groups as names rather than active chemical sites.
misconceptions.fix: A functional group is a specific group of atoms that determines the characteristic chemical reactions of an organic compound.

probe.question: Will ethanol and ethane have similar chemical reactivity because they both contain carbon?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, they are both hydrocarbons so they will react the same way.

misconceptions.statement: Soap molecules dissolve dirt by chemically reacting with it to destroy it.
misconceptions.why: Students view cleaning as a chemical destruction process rather than a physical removal process.
misconceptions.fix: Soap molecules form micelles that trap oil and dirt, allowing them to be washed away by water through physical suspension.

probe.question: How does soap clean a greasy stain?
probe.wrong_answer: The soap chemically burns or breaks down the grease into smaller pieces.
